title: Refactor: Dedicated autoscaler fleet utilization & burst controls reporting
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Refactor autoscaler reporting pipeline: improves fleet utilization accuracy, decouples burst token-bucket metrics from utilization rollups, and adds feature-flagged rollout for dashboards. No customer-facing API changes expected.
description: Context & motivation: The existing fleet utilization and burst controls reporting paths had grown entangled over multiple iterative fixes, causing duplicated aggregation logic, inconsistent windows between burst and utilization metrics, and occasional spikes in dashboard noise. This made it hard to reason about autoscaler behavior and slowed down rollout of priority-based throttles. This PR refactors the reporting pipeline to: 1) centralize core aggregation logic under observability/metrics/fleet_aggregator, 2) separate token-bucket/burst telemetry into a discrete stream so burst smoothing and tokenbucket tuning don't affect utilization rollups, 3) introduce a migration path and feature flags so dashboards can be switched to the new rollups gradually. Changes in this PR: - New fleet_aggregator component (golang) that unifies time-windowed rollups, percentile calculations, and safe merging across shards. - Burst telemetry separated into observability/metrics/burst_stream with protobuf change (backwards compatible: old proto fields retained and mapped). - Dashboard-facing metrics renamed with stable aliases (utilization_v2 while keeping util_v1 alias) to allow A/B. - Added end-to-end tests for aggregation correctness and a small DB migration to add a 'rollup_version' column. - Feature-flag support using existing rollout service; default remains on v1 until gradual enablement. Checklist: - [x] Centralized aggregation implemented and unit tested - [x] Burst telemetry separated and validated against historical data - [x] All dashboards wired to aliases and smoke-tested in staging - [x] Migration script included and reversible - [x] Feature flag added with safe default - [x] Documentation updated for SRE and Dashboard owners Notes on compatibility: The protobuf change is additive; consumers that don't opt-in to v2 will still receive util_v1 metrics. Stream names are backwards-compatible; this PR introduces aliases and a migration plan. Rollout plan: enable v2 rollups in staging for 24h, compare 99th/95th latency and fleet utilization with historical, then enable Canary on 5% of production traffic for 48h, monitor regression alerts. If no regression, ramp to 50% then 100%.
commits_summary: 5 commits: 1) centralize fleet aggregation and add tests; 2) separate burst telemetry stream and protos; 3) add migration and rollup_version column; 4) docs and dashboard wiring; 5) feature flag and rollout config
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Great cleanup - centralizing aggregation makes the logic much easier to follow. A couple of nits on naming and one question about time-window boundary handling.
Sofia Martinez: Thanks! Addressed the naming nits and added explicit window-boundary tests to aggregator_test.go. See commit 'fix: add window boundary tests'.
Priya Desai: Concerned about the on-disk migration during peak traffic. Can we run migration in offline-safe mode and verify both rollup versions in parallel first?

Sofia Martinez: Migration is written to be reversible and runs in a background job. Added a 'parallel_rollup' mode behind the feature flag that keeps both rollups for 48h; updated docs and rollout plan.
Chen Zhao: CI showed a flaky TestAggregator_P95 on first run; reran and it passed. Please add a short timeout/seed to stabilize the test.
Sofia Martinez: Added deterministic seed and tightened timing in the test. CI rerun passed.
ci_checks: E2E (limited): passed after rerun (one flaky test fixed)
notes: Follow-up items: (1) add a small jobs dashboard to track rollup_version adoption per region, (2) run a 72h canary for priority-routing workloads. Owners: SRE (Priya) and Autoscaler (Sofia).
changelog_entry: refactor(autoscaler): centralize fleet rollups, separate burst telemetry, and add feature-flagged v2 rollups. Improves accuracy and paves way for priority-based throughput guarantees.
